description: Evidence-graded catalog of external tools and platforms used across the GenAI career lifecycle: one record per tool or tightly defined tool class, with what it does, a verdict from the rubric, the evidence behind the verdict, its grade, a line-level session citation and the date the evidence was retrieved. 'stage' uses the repository's folder numbers: 0 cross-stage, 1 landscape, 2 roles, 3 skills, 4 certifications, 5 portfolio, 6 job search, 7 networking, 8 interviewing, 9 compensation, 10 onboarding, 11 tracks.
basis: Built from the tool catalogs, findings and operating rules of the October 2026 research sessions. The main source is T0-10, the 12-stage tooling audit (retrieved 2026-10-21); T0-04, T0-05, T0-11, T0-13, T0-14, T0-02, T0-17, T0-07, T0-18, T0-06, T0-09, T0-08 and T1-03 add the tools of their domains. No tool was tested hands-on: verdicts rest on vendor documentation, pricing pages, reviews, datasets and studies as each session graded them, so no verdict validates outcomes. Verdicts follow the sessions. T0-10 Recommended maps to use, Viable to use-with-care and Avoid to avoid. T0-10 Caution maps to use-with-care when the session names a safe use or control, to watch when the blocker is newness or unverified status, and to avoid where the sessions' operating rules say not to rely on it: products whose core function is auto-applying (rejected by T0-04 R6 and T0-10.F4) and LLM career or salary advice. Explicit 'skip' or 'avoid' verdicts in T0-05 and T0-18 also map to avoid. Where sessions conflict, the record says so and takes the more cautious verdict. 'evidence' is the weakest grade among the claims in 'why', on the cited session's own A-D scale (A primary or measured, B transparent secondary, C vendor, third-party or single-source, D recall or judgement); C and D claims are attributed in the text. 'as_of' is the earliest retrieval date among the cited sources; re-verify statuses and prices within 90 days of it. Out of scope by design: communities, including Blind (career/07-networking/communities-guide.md); credentials themselves, including T0-10's certification rows, and engineering frameworks (both in data/skills_ontology.json); and employer-side systems that candidates do not choose (ATSs, AI screening layers, engineering-analytics tools). Beyz and Interviews by AI are omitted because T0-10 found no evidence about them (grade E). Records apply research/ERRATA.md U13, U16 and U17. Tax, visa and legal entries are pointers, not advice.

rubric.use: Default choice for its job. The session recommends it, or it is the official or primary source for that job, and no documented data, billing, terms or stability risk argues against it. Check prices and dates before paying.
rubric.use-with-care: Usable within the control or limit stated in 'why'. Evidence of benefit is thin, vendor-only or unvalidated, or a manageable risk applies (data exposure, billing pattern, platform terms, stability).
rubric.avoid: Do not use for the purpose named. A hard disqualifier applies (a regulator or court finding of deception, a core function that breaches a platform's terms, undisclosed live assistance in an assessed setting, or shutdown without export), or a session explicitly rejects it for that use (for example mass or unattended auto-apply, exam dumps, acting on an LLM's salary number, or paid tooling a session judges unnecessary at job-seeker scale).
rubric.watch: Not assessable yet: new, in beta, changing ownership, or with existence, pricing or behaviour that the sessions could not verify or that conflict, and no safe default use is stated. Do not rely on it; re-check before use.

tools.name: General LLM assistants as career or salary adviser
tools.what: Asking a chat assistant which career to choose or what salary to request, and acting on its figure.
tools.why: Peer-reviewed work (PLOS ONE 2025) and October 2026 preprints auditing 2026-era models (COI: Claude included) confirm persona-dependent salary-advice bias persists. Take pay anchors from independent benchmarks instead.

tools.name: General LLM assistants for drafting and rehearsal (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and similar)
tools.what: Chat assistants used to structure résumé material, draft notes and rehearse interviews, with human verification.
tools.why: A Management Science (2025) field experiment found non-generative writing help raised hires by 8% and wages by 10% on one online labour market; however, Huntr reports most surveyed AI users saw invented details. Verify every claim and never hide prompt-injection text.

tools.name: ChatGPT Atlas
tools.what: Former standalone OpenAI macOS agentic browser.
tools.why: Discontinued on 2026-08-09 and folded into ChatGPT (live-verified 2026-11-19); researchers also demonstrated cross-site prompt-injection data extraction against agentic browsers.
tools.status: closed: discontinued 2026-08-09 and folded into ChatGPT

tools.name: General browser agents for job applying (Comet, Claude in Chrome, Gemini in Chrome)
tools.what: Browser-controlling AI agents clicking and filling web forms across job portals.
tools.why: No job board checked sanctions browser agents for applying, agent blocking rates are rising per HUMAN Security May 2026 data, and cross-site prompt-injection risks apply (COI noted for Claude in Chrome).

tools.name: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook and Employment Projections
tools.what: US government occupational profiles and 2025-35 employment projections (released 2026-08-27, USDL-26-1422).
tools.why: Official and free; supersedes the 2024-34 series. Projects 2025-35 employment growth of +34.6% for data scientists and +21.8% for computer and information research scientists. Downgraded to B from T0-27's Extract-only Grade A (corroborated via web search 2026-11-19).

tools.name: BLS Public Data API
tools.what: Official US Bureau of Labor Statistics API for OEWS wages, CPS and JOLTS series.
tools.why: Official and free; a registered v2 key permits 500 queries per day and 50 series per query across 20 years (key renewed yearly). US labour series only; no live job-posting counts.

tools.name: Epoch AI Frontier Lab Hiring Dataset
tools.what: Daily scrape of Anthropic careers and OpenAI Ashby boards (7-day publication delay) with LLM-assigned role categories.
tools.why: Useful Grade B cross-check for frontier-lab hiring scale (674 Anthropic, 822 OpenAI roles as of 2026-11-06), though all functions are pooled and categories are LLM-assigned.

tools.name: Huntr Job Search Trends reports
tools.what: Quarterly vendor reports on application volume, board conversion and ATS share from Huntr users' self-tracked logs.
tools.why: Large datasets (Q1 2026: 139,927 apps; Q3 2026: 84,753 apps; median 102 days to first offer), including a Q3 within-person Google-vs-LinkedIn check (9.0% vs 2.7%, n=189). Still vendor-run, self-tracked and correlational, with medians restated between editions.

tools.name: Indeed Hiring Lab job postings tracker
tools.what: Open CC-BY-4.0 GitHub dataset of daily job-posting indices refreshed weekly.
tools.why: Primary dataset read directly on GitHub (updated 2026-11-12, CC-BY-4.0 licence). Useful for macro hiring trends across covered countries, but contains no India series.

tools.name: O*NET OnLine, My Next Move and O*NET Web Services
tools.what: Official US occupation skills, tasks and technologies database plus free developer API.
tools.why: Official and free; O*NET Web Services permits publication with attribution, site registration and unaltered data. Because BLS released 2025-35 projections on 2026-08-27, check whether O*NET pages still cite 2024-34 projections; US occupations only.

tools.name: Canada Positive LMIA Employers List
tools.what: Quarterly Open Government Portal dataset of Canadian employers issued positive LMIAs.
tools.why: Official and free, but a historical LMIA is not an open job offer and Canada trimmed Global Talent Stream referral partners in September 2026. Downgraded from T0-27 Extract-only Grade A to B (corroborated 2026-11-19).

tools.name: Denmark SIRI Certified Companies (Fast-track)
tools.what: Official Danish immigration roster of Fast-track certified employers with CVR numbers.
tools.why: Official public register (982 firms reported in press) for accelerated Fast-track permits; Denmark also opens a new work route covering India from 2027-01-01. Downgraded from T0-27 Extract-only Grade A to B (corroborated 2026-11-19).

tools.name: IND Public Register of Recognised Sponsors (Netherlands)
tools.what: Official Dutch Immigration and Naturalisation Service register of recognised visa sponsors.
tools.why: Official and free, updated monthly per IND summary; required for Highly Skilled Migrant sponsorship. Downgraded from T0-27 Extract-only Grade A to B (corroborated via web search 2026-11-19).

tools.name: USCIS H-1B Employer Data Hub
tools.what: Official US employer-level H-1B petition approval and denial lookup by fiscal year.
tools.why: Official dataset, but experienced a five-day outage with reported missing data in March 2026 and bot-blocked automated access in T0-27; cross-check against US DOL OFLC LCA files.

tools.name: roadmap.sh
tools.what: Free, open-source role and skill roadmaps.
tools.why: Free, open-source checklists (AI Engineer and Engineering Manager roadmaps, site updated 2026-09-17), but no hands-on exercises or assessments and no outcome data. T0-68 scores its Engineering Manager roadmap 53/100 (watch); use only as a topic index.

tools.name: Free GPU notebooks (Google Colab free tier, Hugging Face ZeroGPU)
tools.what: Browser-hosted free GPU runtimes for small experiments.
tools.why: Narrower than older assumptions: Colab Pro for Education and AWS SageMaker Studio Lab are closed to new users, and HF ZeroGPU caps free accounts at 5 minutes/day. Suitable for quick prototypes only.
tools.status: changed: Colab Pro for Education and SageMaker Studio Lab closed to new users

tools.name: Free LLM API tiers (Google AI Studio, Groq, OpenRouter, Cerebras)
tools.what: Rate-limited free API endpoints for prototyping and small eval runs.
tools.why: Useful for early API-first prototyping without GPU rental, but rate limits are per-model/per-project and volatile, and flagship models were reported as paid-only from April 2026. Check data-retention/training terms before sending private inputs.

tools.name: Lambda (lambda.ai)
tools.what: On-demand H100 and A100 instances for serving or fine-tuning labs.
tools.why: On-demand H100 SXM rose from $2.99-3.29 in older snapshots to ~$3.99-4.29/hr (single tracker $4.59 in early Nov 2026; cluster configs vary $2.50-3.99; live-verified 2026-11-19). Use H100s only for short labs and verify live prices.

tools.name: Modal
tools.what: Serverless CPU and GPU platform billed per second, used for GPU labs and small deployed endpoints.
tools.why: Starter plan carries $30/month credit (~7.6 H100-hours at ~$3.95/hr; T4 ~$0.59/hr, L4 ~$0.80/hr; live-verified 2026-11-19). Strong for intermittent GPU demos and labs; check live rates before heavy runs.

tools.name: RunPod
tools.what: Rented GPU pods billed per minute, for longer experiments than notebooks allow.
tools.why: RunPod repriced Secure Cloud twice in Sep-Oct 2026: RTX 4090 is ~$0.34/hr Community Cloud and $0.89/hr Secure Cloud (up from $0.69; live-verified 2026-11-19). Re-check live pricing monthly.

tools.name: BlueDot Impact courses (AI Safety, Frontier AI Governance, AGI Strategy)
tools.what: Free facilitated cohort courses (~25 hours) on AI alignment, governance and strategy.
tools.why: Free, updated for 2026, and rated 'use' in T0-68 for Governance, Safety and Leadership families where few independently rated syllabi exist. No independent hiring-outcome data.

tools.name: Claude Academy (formerly Anthropic Academy) [COI]
tools.what: Free vendor courses (22-26 courses, renamed Aug 2026) covering Claude API, agents, MCP and AI fluency.
tools.why: COI (Anthropic product): free and current for Anthropic's stack, with attendance-style certificates. Cross-check against independent multi-provider documentation; no outcome data.

tools.name: Coursera (including Udemy after the merger)
tools.what: MOOC and certificate marketplace; Coursera and Udemy completed their merger in May 2026.
tools.why: Coursera and Udemy completed their merger on 11 May 2026, followed by workforce reductions in July and November 2026 (~10%, live-verified 2026-11-19); catalogue and pricing remain in flux. No independent GenAI course ROI exists (the one causal study covers general degree-less earners in developing countries).
tools.status: merged: Coursera-Udemy completed 2026-05-11; ~10% workforce layoffs Jul and Nov 2026

tools.name: DataTalks.Club LLM Zoomcamp
tools.what: Free, cohort-style course on retrieval-augmented generation that ends in a portfolio project.
tools.why: Free, 10-week cohort-style course (2026-06-08 cohort) with graded capstone project and evaluation module; part of T0-68's free minimal set for Applied AI Engineering (alongside ML/MLOps Zoomcamps). No independent outcome audit.

tools.name: DeepLearning.AI courses and certificates
tools.what: Short courses and specialisations; certificates are course-completion records with public verification pages.
tools.why: Course videos are free; hands-on labs, quizzes and unproctored completion certificates require Pro ($25/mo billed annually at $300/yr, or $30/mo monthly; live-verified 2026-11-19). Useful for structured walkthroughs, but certificates carry no independent hiring ROI.

tools.name: freeCodeCamp
tools.what: Free coding curriculum run by a nonprofit.
tools.why: Free, but T0-10 rated it viable from recall only (not verified in-session), and no ROI evidence was found for any MOOC.

tools.name: GPU MODE lectures and community
tools.what: Free practitioner lecture series and kernel-engineering exercises covering CUDA, Triton and GPU performance.
tools.why: Free, current practitioner-led systems/kernel material rated 'use' in T0-68 alongside T0-12's depth-community recommendation. No outcome audit.

tools.name: Hugging Face Learn
tools.what: Free structured courses on LLMs, agents, MCP and post-training (smol), plus a cookbook.
tools.why: Free, official, runnable courses across LLMs, Agents (with free unproctored certificate after Unit 1, use case and final challenge), MCP and post-training (smol). Note: Robotics (LeRobot) course is a partial release (use-with-care, gate G5). No independent hiring-outcome data.

tools.name: Kaggle (Learn courses and notebooks)
tools.what: Free micro-courses and free GPU notebooks for practice and small experiments.
tools.why: Free 16 GB-class GPU notebooks with 12h GPU/CPU sessions; the often-quoted 30 GPU-hour weekly quota is still not stated in official docs. Useful for small experiments and learning, but competition ranks carry no independent hiring-outcome evidence without documented engineering.

tools.name: NPTEL / SWAYAM
tools.what: Free IIT/IISc faculty courses with optional ₹1,000 in-person proctored exams across India.
tools.why: Two orders of magnitude cheaper than ₹1.3–2.3L ed-tech CEP participation bundles while providing real in-person exam proctoring.

tools.name: NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute (DLI)
tools.what: NVIDIA workshops and courses; DLI workshop certificates are separate from the proctored NVIDIA-Certified exams.
tools.why: Updated October 2026 catalogue replaces stale 2019-2021 snapshots: free Physical AI courses (Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, GR00T) rate strongly, while paid self-paced DLI courses ($30/$90) are strictly non-refundable (live-verified 2026-11-19). Use free content first; DLI certificates are separate from proctored NVIDIA-Certified exams.

tools.name: Stanford CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
tools.what: Free open university course (Spring 2026, 18 lectures and 5 implementation-heavy assignments) covering tokenisation, systems, scaling and alignment.
tools.why: Primary university material updated Spring 2026 (live-verified 2026-11-19); T0-68's highest-rated free systems/LLM curriculum. No independent job-outcome audit.

tools.name: UK AISI Inspect AI documentation
tools.what: Open-source evaluation framework documentation for building reproducible LLM and agent evaluation harnesses.
tools.why: Primary open-source evaluation harness docs rated 'use' in T0-68 for Evaluation, Safety & Security and Human Data transitions; vendor-neutral as hosted eval platforms consolidate or shut down.

tools.name: Codesmith
tools.what: High-ticket software engineering bootcamp ($22,500) that added AI/ML modules.
tools.why: Only bootcamp in T0-68 with a CIRR independent audit (2023 software cohort: 43.6% placed in-field at 180 days, 70.1% at 12 months; live-verified 2026-11-19), **but** that audited cohort predates its AI/ML syllabus and tuition is $22,500. Do not project 2023 SWE outcomes onto 2026 GenAI roles.

tools.name: High-fee Indian institute CEP / ed-tech certificate bundles (₹1.3–2.3L)
tools.what: Co-branded IIT/IISc/IIIT continuing-education GenAI programmes sold via Jaro, TalentSprint, TimesPro and InterviewBit.
tools.why: Issue non-refundable certificates of participation (not degrees, no placement guarantee) with 0/14 India posting hits; consumer commissions ruled against Eduonix and Simplilearn. Use only if employer-sponsored for structured instruction, never for job-search ROI.

tools.name: Income-share-agreement bootcamps (BloomTech/Lambda School model)
tools.what: Paid bootcamps financed by a share of future income instead of up-front tuition.
tools.why: Hard disqualifier: CFPB consent order (2024-04-17) found BloomTech misrepresented ISAs as non-loans and inflated placement claims; California BPPE confirms final instruction 31 Dec 2025. Treat ISA, pay-after-placement and EMI schemes as loans; no Indian ISA provider has audited outcomes.
tools.status: closed: BloomTech final day of instruction 2025-12-31 (California BPPE)

tools.name: India paid AI bootcamps & executive tracks (Scaler, upGrad/IIIT-B, Great Learning, Simplilearn, Interview Kickstart)
tools.what: High-ticket paid AI/ML programmes (₹1.25L-₹3.99L / $2,499-$4,800; Interview Kickstart unpublished).
tools.why: No independent audited GenAI placement outcomes exist. Refund terms diverge sharply (Scaler 14d from first class; upGrad pre-start only; Simplilearn admin deduction / 7d Wharton; Interview Kickstart conditional 50% or none on listed Indian tracks), and EMI/NBFC financing behaves like a loan. Verify written refund and lender terms before paying; free minimal sets cover every role family.

tools.name: Maven AI Evals cohort
tools.what: Live 6-week practitioner-led cohort on LLM evaluation (33 sessions).
tools.why: Highest-scoring paid course in T0-68 (75-80 before gates), but capped by gate G2: tuition rose from ~$3,000 (2025) to $4,200 (Oct 2026, announced as last 2026 cohort; live-verified 2026-11-19), no independent outcome audit exists, and Week-2 refund timing needs confirmation against a full 14-day window. Consider only if employer-funded after building an eval harness v0.

tools.name: Vendor-awarded 'Certified AI Consultant / Fractional CAIO' badges (e.g. chiefaiofficer.com)
tools.what: Unassessed 3-day to 10-week vendor-awarded executive AI consultant/CAIO credentials.
tools.why: Fails T0-68 gate G4: vendor-awarded title with undisclosed pricing and zero independent assessment or employer recognition.

tools.name: Anthropic Partner Academy (Skilljar)
tools.what: Portal governing Claude Partner Network exams (Pearson VUE) and partner tier discounts.
tools.why: Closed to non-partners; CCAO-F excluded from tiers; 5 changes in 8 months plus V0 US DoW FASCSA exclusion risk.

tools.name: Certiverse (NVIDIA exam delivery)
tools.what: Remote-proctored exam platform for NVIDIA Associate and Professional AI certifications.
tools.why: Verify live seat availability inside Certiverse before paying for study materials because NVIDIA pages showed '(Coming soon)' tags for NCP-GENL and NCP-AAI.

tools.name: LangChain Academy & Talview
tools.what: Free prep courses and $99 live dual-camera proctored LCAE exam with live LangSmith trace workspace and 1 free resit.
tools.why: Only open-enrolment paid proctored agent-framework exam verified in T0-29; note strict secondary-camera room-scan requirement.

tools.name: Official certification portals (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Learn, Databricks, NVIDIA)
tools.what: Vendors' own exam pages and guides: fees, formats, validity, recommended experience and retirement notices.
tools.why: The primary source for every exam fact. Check retirement notices before booking: AWS Machine Learning – Specialty had its last exam on 31 Mar 2026, and Azure AI-102 retired on 30 Jun 2026 (successor AI-103, whose exam page carried a beta label).

tools.name: Unverified private AI certification bodies (ARTiBA, GSDC, Blockchain Council, IABAC, USAII)
tools.what: Commercial AI exam sellers charging $150–$1,450 without independently verifiable accreditation.
tools.why: Zero verified accreditation (GSDC cites ISO/IEC 17024 PCB-168 without naming the accreditation body), 0/29 US+India posting hits, and exam-dump listings found for USAII.

tools.name: Accredible
tools.what: Public digital credential verification registry used by LangChain (LCAE), Snowflake (SnowPro) and OpenAI Partner Network.
tools.why: Provides verifiable public badge links alongside Credly for résumé and LinkedIn proof.

tools.name: Credly
tools.what: Public badge verification used by AWS and Google Cloud certifications.
tools.why: Public badge links show active or expired status. T0-11 advises listing the full credential name, exam code, issue and expiry dates and a public Credly link on the résumé. Pearson owns Credly and also delivers exams through Pearson VUE.

tools.name: Exam-dump sites
tools.what: Sites selling leaked or reconstructed certification exam questions.
tools.why: Dump material for AWS MLA-C01 is sold openly in 2026, and relying on it destroys the only thing a multiple-choice credential signals. No independent cheating-rate measurement exists for AWS, Google or Microsoft exams.

tools.name: Linux Foundation Training & Killer.sh
tools.what: Delivers hands-on Kubernetes exams (CKA, CKAD, CKS) with 2x36h Killer.sh simulator attempts, plus PTCA and MCPA.
tools.why: High hands-on rigour and transparent KCSP partner value for CKA; every exam purchase includes one retake.

tools.name: Anthropic Console workspace spend limits
tools.what: Per-workspace monthly spend and rate limits under the organisation cap.
tools.why: The Default Workspace cannot be capped, and workspace limits sit below the organisation limit; create a dedicated named workspace per demo or project (COI disclosed in T0-13 and T0-20).

tools.name: OpenAI project spend limits
tools.what: Organisation and project monthly limits on OpenAI API spend.
tools.why: Enable 'Enforce a hard limit' so excess calls return HTTP 429; alerts alone do not stop billing. Because enforcement is not instantaneous, pair with application-level rate limits and a daily budget counter.

tools.name: git log on a treeless or blobless clone
tools.what: Local, unmetered repository-history analysis of committing employer domains.
tools.why: Plain git log needs only commits on a treeless clone (--filter=tree:0), but path-filtered git log downloads trees for almost every commit; GitHub advises against treeless clones for daily use and recommends blobless clones (--filter=blob:none) for history queries. Never harvest emails (prohibited by GitHub AUP).

tools.name: GitHub GraphQL API
tools.what: Programmatic access to public repository and contributor metadata.
tools.why: Free at 5,000 points/hour per user (1,000/hour per repository for GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions). GitHub's AUP ('Services Usage Limits', section 6 in T0-20 extract) bars unsolicited email and selling personal data to recruiters/job boards, and ties public-data research use to open-access publication.

tools.name: OSS Insight
tools.what: Free GitHub event analytics with a data explorer and public REST API.
tools.why: Free access over 5+ billion rows of public GitHub events to inspect which employers staff candidate repositories. Company attributions are inferred from public profiles, so treat tables as approximate.

tools.name: GitHub profile and GitHub Pages
tools.what: Code hosting and free static-site hosting from public repositories.
tools.why: Free for public repositories up to 1 GB with soft limits of 100 GB/month bandwidth and 10 builds/hour; prohibits commercial or SaaS use. Keep source exportable on a domain you own (Read.cv shut down within four months of acquisition) and never commit secrets.

tools.name: Hugging Face Spaces
tools.what: Hosting for ML demos: static sites, Gradio and Docker apps, and optional paid GPUs.
tools.why: Official docs (read in full) confirm static Spaces stay free while Gradio and Docker Spaces on compute require PRO (US$9/month on HF pages, which also bundles profile blog publishing) or Team/Enterprise. Free accounts get up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces; free hardware sleeps when idle, and a paid T4 small left on 30 days costs about US$288.
tools.status: changed: Gradio and Docker Spaces on compute require PRO (US$9/month); older tutorials say they are free

tools.name: Railway
tools.what: Usage-billed application hosting.
tools.why: Free plan gives a US$1 monthly credit; Hobby is US$5/month (minimum due even if unused, includes US$5 of usage); Pro is US$20/month. Viable for a modest live-demo budget, though free credits cover little.

tools.name: Read.cv
tools.what: Former professional profile and portfolio-site platform.
tools.why: Hard disqualifier D4: acquired by Perplexity on 2025-01-17 and wound down with export closing on 2025-05-16. Keep portfolio and writing canonical on exportable, own-domain hosting.
tools.status: closed: acquired by Perplexity 2025-01-17; export closed 2025-05-16

tools.name: Replicate
tools.what: Hosted model-running API platform.
tools.why: Acquisition by Cloudflare was announced 2025-11-17 and closed 2025-12-01; product roadmap and pricing may change, and T0-13's demo hosting tree omits it.
tools.status: acquired: by Cloudflare, announced 2025-11-17 and closed 2025-12-01

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.what: CI and scheduled jobs that re-run tests and capped evaluations.
tools.why: Standard hosted runners remain free for public repositories; larger runners are paid, and a proposed US$0.002/min self-hosted runner platform fee announced in December 2025 was postponed (not cancelled). Put per-run spend caps on workflows calling paid LLM APIs.

tools.name: Shields.io endpoint badges
tools.what: README badges fed by public JSON generated in CI.
tools.why: Endpoint JSON requires schemaVersion 1, label and message; cache values below 300 seconds are ignored. A badge is only self-asserted (V0) unless it links directly to the CI run or raw result file that produced it.

tools.name: Indeed Career Scout
tools.what: First-party Indeed AI career coach and job-matching assistant.
tools.why: Launched in the US in September 2025 with an India preview announced; all outcome claims are vendor-only (COI) and India rollout status is unverified.

tools.name: santifer/career-ops (open source)
tools.what: MIT-licensed local AI job-search pipeline that scans, scores and tailors PDFs without auto-submitting.
tools.why: Active open-source project (82,242 stars, last commit 2026-11-12) that enforces human-in-the-loop submission by design. However, built-in board scanning may breach site terms; restrict to permitted endpoints and ignore contact scraping.

tools.name: Ashby AI-Assisted Application Review
tools.what: Opt-in employer screening layer grading each recruiter criterion Meets, Does not meet, unknown or skipped with citations and sortable criteria-met %; FairNow audit Aug 2024.
tools.why: Assistive rather than a documented rejecter (separate rule-based auto-reject runs on form answers), but blank long-form answers are marked Not Met and unreadable files Skipped. Never leave long-form questions blank.

tools.name: Eightfold Match Score
tools.what: Employer AI ranking score (0-5 in half-point steps with explanations) sorting candidate lists; BLDS Morgan Stanley audit covered 1,332,869 applicant records (2025-06 to 2026-05).
tools.why: Documented as advisory (Morgan Stanley calls it one factor); impact ratios in BLDS audit measure above-median share (~31-32%), not recruiter reading order. Subject to pending FCRA consumer-report motion to dismiss in Kistler v. Eightfold AI.

tools.name: Greenhouse Talent Matching (Real Talent)
tools.what: Employer AI triage categorising applicants (Strong, Good, Partial, Limited, Needs manual review) at initial review; NYC LL144 audit dated 2026-07-30.
tools.why: Documented as no auto-reject or auto-advance; unreadable résumés and per-application candidate opt-outs (where employer-enabled) route to manual review and delete AI scores. Opt-out speed effect is untested; keep a record if opting out.

tools.name: Kula AI Scoring and fraud detector
tools.what: Employer AI screening layer assigning numeric match scores with an optional minimum-score auto-reject threshold and optional fraud-flag auto-reject (both off by default; updated 2026-08-19).
tools.why: A primary vendor-documented exception showing that 'AI never auto-rejects' is unsafe to assume (updates T0-04.F1 / K1). Ensure clean extraction and explicit evidence lines per requirement.

tools.name: LinkedIn Hiring Assistant
tools.what: Recruiter-facing AI sourcing and shortlisting agent (launch reported Sep 2025); vendor claims recruiters review 81% fewer profiles and states no autonomous decisions.
tools.why: Vendor-claimed 81% drop in profiles reviewed (COI) illustrates visibility risk: candidates not surfaced may never be opened. Keep LinkedIn skills, titles and dates complete and aligned with your portal résumé.

tools.name: Phenom Fit Score
tools.what: Employer AI fit score for recruiter triage across skills, experience, title and location; third-party bias audit published in 2024.
tools.why: Audit PDF exists, but scoring weights and any auto-reject behaviour were not verified in T0-47 (audit not read in full).
tools.status: unverified: 2024 bias audit PDF not read in full in T0-47

tools.name: Workday HiredScore (Spotlight, Fetch) and Candidate Skills Match
tools.what: Employer AI screening layer grading parsed profiles A-D against basic and preferred qualifications, with opt-in LLM fit-and-gap mode (production 2026-08-07).
tools.why: Documented as advisory (vendor says no auto-reject; Secretariat audit published by Thomson Reuters), while the Mobley v. Workday order (2025-05-16; hearing 2027-03-09) left auto-rejection open. Cover every basic qualification explicitly and type Skills/Languages in Workday.

tools.name: Jobscan
tools.what: Résumé-to-posting Match Rate scanner (over 30 checks, weightings unpublished).
tools.why: Jobscan's own page calls Match Rate its own visualisation, not an employer's ATS score. No validation links checker scores to outcomes; an 8-scanner test scored one 612-word PDF from 54 to 91. Use only as a gap list against a posting, never a pass/fail gate. Premium about $49.95/month.

tools.name: Resume Worded
tools.what: Résumé feedback giving a 0-100 score from 20+ checks in Impact, Brevity and Style.
tools.why: Vendor score guide (updated July 2026) opened directly: claims to simulate recruiters and ATS extraction are unverified, and the page gives no outcome data. Treat the score as a gap list, never an ATS gate.

tools.name: Resume-Matcher (open source)
tools.what: Apache-2.0 local LLM gap-analysis and résumé-matching tool.
tools.why: Active open-source local alternative (29,270 stars, last commit 2026-11-07) avoiding cloud uploads; treat match scores strictly as a posting gap list because no checker score predicts ATS outcomes.

tools.name: MyGreenhouse
tools.what: Greenhouse's free global candidate profile, tracker and Quick Apply autofill.
tools.why: Primary vendor page verified: free and global for Greenhouse-hosted roles, with human submit. Your profile may be recommended to hiring teams unless you opt out; outcome claims are vendor-only.

tools.name: Simplify Copilot
tools.what: Free browser extension autofilling ATS application forms with human submission.
tools.why: Human-submit autofill (~500k Chrome users) on employer ATS pages; however, Firefox listing requests all-sites data access and the same account includes Simplify Autopilot. Keep Autopilot off and avoid running on LinkedIn or Indeed.

tools.name: Huntr (tracker and job clipper)
tools.what: Application tracker and browser clipper with AI add-ons.
tools.why: Free tier (100 jobs per third party) covers tracking; Pro is $40/month, $90/quarter or $160 per six months. Watch multi-month upfront billing and unretrieved extension permissions.

tools.name: Teal
tools.what: Job application tracker, résumé builder and keyword-match checker.
tools.why: Free tier covers core tracking. Primary help centre confirms Teal+ rose to $13/week, $29/month or $79/quarter (superseding $9/week); avoid weekly auto-renew and treat its match score as a gap list only.

tools.name: AIHawk and open-source LinkedIn auto-apply bots
tools.what: Open-source auto-apply bots (AIHawk 32,498 stars; Auto_job_applier_linkedIn 3,031 stars) and JobSpy scraper (4,709 stars).
tools.why: MIT licences do not override platform terms: core functions automate applying or scraping on LinkedIn and Indeed, violating board rules and exposing accounts to restriction.

tools.name: Hosted cloud auto-apply services (FastApply, LoopCV, JobCopilot, Massive, AIApply)
tools.what: Subscription services whose cloud agents fill in and submit applications for you.
tools.why: Not individually audited; one vendor's own test of eight bots claims only three actually click Submit. Cloud agents likely submit from data-centre IPs, which Greenhouse treats as a high-risk fraud signal (T0-10's inference), and T0-04 R6 rejects mass auto-apply.

tools.name: Indeed Apply For Me
tools.what: First-party Indeed AI drafting and submission feature tested in the US.
tools.why: Tested from 2026-07-07, then Indeed paused the automatic submission mode on 2026-08-04 (trade press cites employer pushback), keeping review-all-drafts (live-verified 2026-11-19).
tools.status: changed: automatic mode paused 2026-08-04; review-all-drafts mode retained

tools.name: Jobscan Auto Apply
tools.what: Application drafting and submission tool bundled with Jobscan Premium ($49.95/month).
tools.why: Verified live: targets Lever and Workable at launch with review by default and optional auto-submit. No independent outcome evidence exists; keep auto-submit turned off if testing.
tools.status: new: launch reported, not re-verified

tools.name: LazyApply
tools.what: Browser extension that bulk-applies to jobs through job boards.
tools.why: Hard disqualifier D2: LinkedIn's terms prohibit the automation it performs. Trustpilot shows about 2.4/5 on roughly 107 reviews, with wrong answers, off-target applications and refund complaints, and T0-04 R6 rejects mass auto-apply.

tools.name: Scoutify (alerts and 'Sniper' auto-apply)
tools.what: Job alerts plus a career-site auto-apply mode.
tools.why: The only evidence is the vendor's own blog (T0-10 Caution; about $5, $15 or $25 a week, vendor-stated), and T0-10 relied on that blog for other tools. Its auto-apply mode falls under T0-04 R6, which rejects auto-apply.

tools.name: Simplify Autopilot
tools.what: Credit-based unattended application submission agent bundled in Simplify+.
tools.why: Primary help pages confirm 20 credits/week and no review step before submission (stops only when unable to determine an answer); third parties report Simplify+ at $19.99/wk, $39.99/mo or $89.99/qtr. Avoid unattended submission.
tools.status: changed: help centre dropped beta label; homepage labels early access

tools.name: Sonara (relaunched under BOLD)
tools.what: Cloud auto-apply service.
tools.why: The original service shut down on 1 Feb 2024, and the brand was reportedly relaunched under BOLD, per competitor sources. T0-10 rates it Caution and T0-04 R6 rejects auto-apply.
tools.status: relaunched: original service shut down 1 Feb 2024; brand reportedly relaunched under BOLD

tools.name: CLEAR identity verification (employer-initiated, via Greenhouse)
tools.what: Employer-triggered identity check in MyGreenhouse: government ID, liveness selfie and device/network signals; CLEAR stores ID/selfie and Greenhouse receives pass/fail and basic fields.
tools.why: Free to candidates and optional (you may decline, though the employer decides next steps), with a 14-day window (10 days after starting). Complete only via a verified employer channel, match application details to ID, avoid VPN/proxy and ask what follows a failure; no false-positive rates published.

tools.name: 80,000 Hours job board
tools.what: Hand-curated job board focused on AI safety, security and policy roles.
tools.why: Narrowed specifically to AI-focused roles in July 2026; high curation bar for safety and governance tracks. Not comprehensive, and operator hiring-share claims carry COI (C).

tools.name: Cutshort (India)
tools.what: Independent Indian startup and product-company tech hiring board.
tools.why: Public sample (n=17 employers) was 53% startups or small product firms, and 9 of 18 postings displayed a numeric pay band; spot-check individual ads for quality anomalies.

tools.name: EURAXESS Jobs
tools.what: European Commission portal for academic, PhD, postdoc and AI research positions across 43+ countries.
tools.why: Official public portal where institutions post free; carries LLM-related MSCA fellowships and thousands of European research openings.

tools.name: Fast AI Jobs
tools.what: Curated AI-startup job index pulling from company ATS pages with an H-1B filter.
tools.why: Useful AI-startup ATS index (28,414 roles at 1,824 startups, Aug 2026), but daily refresh is an operator claim (COI); verify on employer boards. Category noise (Nov 2026): 64% of newest AI Engineer rows were Applied AI/FDE and 46-56% of newest FDE rows were non-engineering GTM/strategist roles.

tools.name: foundit (India)
tools.what: General Indian job portal matching search terms across full job-description text.
tools.why: Displayed 23,720 'Generative Ai' results on 2026-11-11, but matches on body text (including non-AI false positives). Public sample (n=36) was 67% IT services and 17% staffing, with pay shown on only 1 of 20 listings.

tools.name: Google Jobs and direct employer career pages
tools.what: Search aggregation routing directly to employer ATS application forms.
tools.why: Highest conversion in Huntr Q1-Q3 2026 (Google-sourced: 7.12%, 7.91%, 9.9%; within-person 9.0% vs 2.7% LinkedIn, n=189), matching Greenhouse's 2025 finding that company boards yield ~3.2x external boards. Always verify recruiter domains.

tools.name: GRC Careers (ai-governance-jobs.com)
tools.what: Specialist job board for AI governance, risk, compliance and assurance roles.
tools.why: Useful specialist discovery surface for governance and risk roles, but carries multi-city duplicates (KPMG x10), almost no engineering titles on its Responsible AI tab (1/48), and boilerplate skill lists across pages (COI).

tools.name: Hacker News 'Who is hiring?' monthly thread
tools.what: Monthly Hacker News thread where company staff post engineering and AI roles directly.
tools.why: Moderation rules restrict posts to company staff (no third-party recruiters or boards) with explicit location and REMOTE/ONSITE tags; verify employer domains before replying.

tools.name: hiring.cafe
tools.what: Free job search engine crawling employer career pages and ATS boards.
tools.why: Redirects directly to employer ATS forms and ranked third by saves in Huntr (7,759 saves to July 2026, no published rate). Advertised totals conflict (2.8M-5.7M across reviews), ghost-job filtering is operator-claimed, and no public API exists.

tools.name: Hirist (Info Edge)
tools.what: Info Edge Indian technology job board with a user base distinct from Naukri.
tools.why: Useful specialist Indian tech board (Pune 335 indexed GenAI listings in Sep 2026; national count script-rendered), but public sample (n=18 employers) was 72% services/analytics rather than startups.

tools.name: iimjobs (Info Edge)
tools.what: Info Edge management and senior-hiring job board in India.
tools.why: Owned by Info Edge alongside Naukri and Hirist; no GenAI posting volume was located in T0-25 searches.

tools.name: Indeed and Glassdoor (merged inventory) plus Handshake
tools.what: General job aggregators (Glassdoor legally merged into Indeed, Inc. on 2026-07-01) and US campus board Handshake.
tools.why: Treat Indeed and Glassdoor as one shared inventory post-merger (live-verified 2026-11-19). Huntr interview rates: Indeed 3.14% (Q1) and 3.6% (Q3), Glassdoor 2.1% (Jul 2026), Handshake 3.35% (Q1). Indeed explicitly prohibits third-party applying bots.
tools.status: merged: Glassdoor legally merged into Indeed, Inc. on 2026-07-01

tools.name: Inference Jobs
tools.what: Niche aggregator for GPU infrastructure, inference and kernel engineering roles.
tools.why: Useful employer discovery for GPU infra, inference and kernel teams, but carries stale listings up to two years old (~40% <=3 months on page 1) and ~45% OS/driver noise on its GPU Kernel tag.

tools.name: Instahyre (India)
tools.what: Independent Indian employer-initiated tech talent-matching platform.
tools.why: Widely used for Indian tech hiring, but GenAI volume requires login (unmeasured) and its employer-page claim of '40% more premium profiles than Naukri' is promotional and unverifiable.

tools.name: Internshala (India)
tools.what: Indian student and fresher internship and entry-level job board.
tools.why: Useful for fresher GenAI internships and displays stipend fields (bars unpaid internships except named exceptions), but observed GenAI stipends can be low (INR 8,000-11,000/month); never pay to apply.

tools.name: Japan Dev and TokyoDev
tools.what: Curated English-friendly Japanese tech and AI job boards with visa-sponsorship filters.
tools.why: Explicit 'Apply from abroad' / visa-sponsor and 'Japan residents only' filters plus yen salary ranges (live-verified 2026-11-19). Downgraded from T0-25 Extract-only Grade A to B.

tools.name: Job Bank (Canada)
tools.what: Official Canadian government NOC-coded job board with international-candidate filters.
tools.why: Free, NOC-coded and flags roles open to international candidates, but mirrors Indeed, Monster and CareerBeacon listings so de-duplication is required. Downgraded from T0-25 Extract-only Grade A to B.

tools.name: Jobgether
tools.what: Remote-focused job board and remote-work flexibility index.
tools.why: Publishes useful cross-border remote shares (4.0% worldwide, 2.1% excluding all-open ATS feeds, Sep 2026; B per D-018), but its India remote AI filter (n=416 on 2026-11-13) included 202 inflated 'anywhere' ATS feeds alongside 209 India-located roles. Always verify eligibility on the employer's own careers page.

tools.name: Jobright.ai
tools.what: US-centric AI job-matching board with a reported application agent.
tools.why: Evidence still comes only from competitor and review posts; pricing conflicts ($20-40/mo reported) and one review saw the pricing page return HTTP 404 on 2026-10-09. Require a primary source before use.
tools.status: unverified: pricing page 404 reported 2026-10-09; competitor sources only

tools.name: JobsPipe
tools.what: Multi-source AI job index and API aggregating 30+ sources with role and skill pages.
tools.why: Indexed 3,944 AI Engineer roles globally (Nov 2026), but re-lists Indeed/LinkedIn and its India sample is consulting-heavy. Title counts stayed frozen 2026-10-19 to 2026-11-13, JD skill shares date from 2026-09-10, and India share differs internally (10.1% live vs 13.6% Sep).

tools.name: LinkedIn Jobs and networking (free tier, manual use)
tools.what: Global job board and professional network, used strictly by hand.
tools.why: High reach for sourcing and referrals, but low application conversion in Huntr Q1-Q3 2026 (2.94%, 3.36%, 3.6%). LinkedIn prohibits automation extensions and scrapers; Texas AG issued a CID on 2026-07-14 over ghost-job and Premium allegations (no lawsuit filed).
tools.status: under investigation: Texas AG CID issued 2026-07-14 (allegations; no lawsuit as of 2026-11-19)

tools.name: MyCareersFuture (Singapore)
tools.what: Singapore government job portal with compulsory salary fields (per third-party statement).
tools.why: Official free portal with strong salary transparency for Singapore roles; press searches noted 150-181 AI engineer listings on undated June snapshots.

tools.name: Naukri (free tier; paid FastForward use-with-care)
tools.what: India's largest job board (Info Edge: 118M résumés, 697,000 listings as of June 2026).
tools.why: Core India volume board (third-party counts 10,953-55,203 GenAI/AI hits; logged-out counts blocked). Use the free tier first: FastForward/Priority Applicant has zero independent outcome evidence, and Naukri warns against fee scams and spoofed domains.

tools.name: OpenAI Jobs Platform
tools.what: AI-company jobs platform announced for mid-2026.
tools.why: Announced for mid-2026, not live in August 2026 evidence and no launch evidence found by 2026-11-11; monitor before relying on it.
tools.status: unverified: announced for mid-2026; no launch evidence found as of 2026-11-11

tools.name: PhysicalAI.jobs
tools.what: Robotics and embodied-AI job aggregator tracking ~4,875 roles across 115 companies.
tools.why: Useful for company discovery in robotics and physical AI (about 20% Embodied AI), heavily weighted to US autonomy and defence rather than pure VLA volume.

tools.name: SimplifyJobs GitHub internship and new-grad lists
tools.what: Community-curated and hourly-scraped GitHub tables of US/Canada tech and AI/ML early-career roles.
tools.why: Includes dedicated AI/ML category with explicit no-sponsorship and US-citizenship flags; strong free index for US and Canada early-career candidates.

tools.name: Welcome to the Jungle (absorbed Otta)
tools.what: Europe and US startup/tech job board routing applicants to employer ATS pages.
tools.why: Huntr interview rates rose across 2026 editions (3.63% Q1, 4.70% Q2, 6.2% Q3; correlational). Strong France coverage (source for 1,602 Ingénieur IA aggregator ads in Oct 2026).

tools.name: Wellfound (including Wellfound India)
tools.what: Startup job board showing posted pay and equity ranges alongside founder contacts.
tools.why: Huntr interview rates of 5.02% (Q1), 5.20% (Q2) and 4.5% (Q3 2026; correlational). India snapshot shows 707 AI Engineer hits (undated) with pay/equity on most listings, though very low bands and stale indexed ads appear.

tools.name: Work at a Startup (Y Combinator)
tools.what: Free startup job board restricted to Y Combinator-backed companies with one shared profile.
tools.why: Restricts postings to YC companies (reducing agency spam) and uses native applications; some listings carry US-citizen or visa-only tags. GenAI counts not observed without login.

tools.name: Adzuna API
tools.what: Official job-search, salary and histogram REST API with free personal keys.
tools.why: Primary Terms of Service opened directly confirm free personal job-search evaluation use (commercial use needs agreement; one account only). Third-party lists include India ('in'), though Adzuna's own country page was not opened.

tools.name: Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby public job-board APIs
tools.what: Unauthenticated per-company GET endpoints exposing public job postings JSON.
tools.why: Documented for public job-board feeds and ideal for low-rate personal company watchlists. Do not republish data: Lever carries an unresolved service-bureau terms clause for third parties and Ashby's API host robots.txt returned 401 on 2026-11-02.

tools.name: Jooble, Remotive and Arbeitnow job APIs
tools.what: Free REST job feeds for broad aggregation (Jooble), remote roles (Remotive) and Europe/remote (Arbeitnow).
tools.why: Official free feeds (Remotive README opened directly: 24-hour delay, max 4 calls/day advised, attribution required); Jooble and Arbeitnow terms texts were not read, and Jooble places API keys in the URL path.

tools.name: USAJOBS API and Reed Jobseeker API
tools.what: Official free REST APIs for US federal jobs (USAJOBS) and UK vacancies (Reed).
tools.why: Official, documented and free for individuals (USAJOBS requires email User-Agent; Reed uses basic auth); narrow geographic scope (US federal and UK only).

tools.name: adzuna-mcp (community)
tools.what: Community MCP wrapper querying Adzuna job search and salary endpoints with your own official API keys.
tools.why: Operates within Adzuna's official personal-use API terms rather than scraping; subject to free-tier rate limits and third-party maintenance.

tools.name: Greenhouse MCP and Workable MCP (official employer-side)
tools.what: Official OAuth MCP servers connecting hiring teams to Greenhouse (open beta Jul 2026) and Workable (94 tools Jul 2026).
tools.why: Built for employer admins and recruiters with workspace OAuth scopes, not for individual job seekers (live-verified 2026-11-19).
tools.status: beta: employer-side recruiting integrations

tools.name: Indeed MCP (official beta)
tools.what: Official Indeed remote MCP server providing read-only job search, job details, résumé read and company data inside Claude.
tools.why: Official and permitted by Indeed (live-verified 2026-11-19 at docs.indeed.com/mcp), but beta, read-only and Claude-only; reads your Indeed profile, and docs list 4 tools while one directory lists 2 (COI: Anthropic/Claude ecosystem).
tools.status: beta: read-only Claude connector

tools.name: stickerdaniel/linkedin-mcp-server and scraper-backed job MCPs
tools.what: Unofficial MCP servers accessing LinkedIn or Indeed via browser session cookies or hosted scrapers (HasData, Apify).
tools.why: No official LinkedIn job-search MCP exists. Community session servers (4,202 stars) import your logged-in browser cookies and can message or connect on your behalf, breaching platform terms and exposing credentials.

tools.name: Greenhouse 'Unsuccessful resume parse' checklist
tools.what: Greenhouse's support article listing conditions that trigger an unsuccessful résumé parse.
tools.why: Vendor-documented trigger list (updated 2026-03-02): files over 2.5 MB, letter-spaced text, graphics, photos, image uploads, complex tables, headers/footers/text boxes, column layouts, placeholder data, unclear sections, incomplete titles, and company names without identifiers. Failed parse leaves fields for manual entry, not rejection.

tools.name: Open-source PDF checks (pdffonts, pdftotext, PyMuPDF, pypdf, pdfminer.six, pdfplumber)
tools.what: Free local checks (pdffonts plus two cross-family text extractors such as pdftotext and PyMuPDF).
tools.why: T0-23 M1 across six extractors confirms two cross-family extractors expose column-order splits (4 of 6 row-by-row vs 2 column-by-column), all six return hidden white text, and only PyMuPDF recovers hyperlink targets. Correction: require a Unicode map on embedded fonts only (standard non-embedded Type 1 fonts show 'no' and still extract).

tools.name: Vendor parser demos (for example Textkernel Extract!)
tools.what: Commercial CV-parser trials and demos (for example Textkernel Extract, 500 free trial credits).
tools.why: Textkernel Extract (modified 2026-04-30) offers 500 free trial credits and parses 29 languages, but its accuracy claim has no independent benchmark, and no major ATS confirms which engine it runs. Do not upload sensitive personal data to a vendor trial.

tools.name: BOLD-family builders (Zety, MyPerfectResume, LiveCareer, Resume Now)
tools.what: Subscription résumé builders in the BOLD LLC family (Zety, MyPerfectResume, LiveCareer, Resume Now).
tools.why: Zety's pricing page shows $1.95 for 14 days then $25.95 every four weeks (currency unlabelled, updating earlier ~$3/$24 reports; annual $71.40). A single news brief reports >5.1M LiveCareer files exposed in an unsecured bucket (C). Set a cancellation reminder and upload Tier 1 data only.

tools.name: Canva résumé templates
tools.what: Design tool whose résumé templates export as PDF (tagged PDFs need PDF Standard, flattening off).
tools.why: Canva's help is still silent on selectable text layers. An Oct 2026 vendor test kept the text layer on one Canva-style PDF but read a sidebar before work history and turned icons into stray characters (earlier 20-template claim withdrawn). Keep for humans; self-test before portals.

tools.name: Enhancv
tools.what: Design-forward online résumé builder with multi-column templates.
tools.why: Enhancv claims multi-column parsing (98% vs 95%, method undisclosed), conflicting with Greenhouse's documented column-layout parse trigger. Pricing page price fields were broken on 2026-11-14; refunds only for error or breakage. Stick to single-column and self-test.

tools.name: Kickresume
tools.what: Online résumé and cover-letter builder.
tools.why: Privacy policy (updated 2026-08-03) lets Kickresume use anonymised user documents to improve services and explicitly states it cannot fully rely on all data being anonymised (allows objection). Upload Tier 1 data only (no home address, date of birth or ID numbers).

tools.name: OpenResume
tools.what: Open-source résumé builder and in-browser PDF.js parser (AGPL-3.0; 8.9k GitHub stars on 2026-11-14).
tools.why: Free local/open-source option, but its ATS-friendly claim cites no verification method or outcome data and its parser reflects PDF.js rather than employer ATS engines. Self-test exports across two extractor families.

tools.name: Reactive Resume (open source)
tools.what: MIT-licensed, self-hostable open-source résumé builder.
tools.why: Actively maintained (45,680 stars, last commit 2026-11-12) and free to self-host for full data control; hosted-service retention terms were not verified.

tools.name: RenderCV (open source)
tools.what: MIT-licensed YAML-to-PDF résumé generator keeping CV content as structured data.
tools.why: Clean CV-as-data default (17,949 stars) that keeps source files portable in your personal repo; slower commit cadence (last commit 2026-03-25 as of 2026-11-13) and still requires a PDF parse check.

tools.name: Resume.io
tools.what: Online résumé builder sold through a 7-day low-price trial.
tools.why: Pricing page shows $2.95 for 7 days converting to $29.95 every four weeks (the FAQ calls it monthly; $49.95 quarterly; currency unlabelled; 7-day money-back guarantee). Set a cancellation reminder before starting the trial.

tools.name: Rezi
tools.what: Résumé builder with a 1-100 Rezi Score across five areas (formula unpublished).
tools.why: Rezi's own documentation (2026-07-16) states that real ATS systems give no official score and recruiters do not see its number. Use as a drafting aid, not a gate. About $29/month or $149 lifetime in roundups.

tools.name: Apollo.io
tools.what: B2B contact lookup database and outreach sequencing.
tools.why: Free tier captured at 900 credits/year (75/month) in September-November 2026 (down from 1,200/year; pages conflict). Not in Pin's finder audit, and LinkedIn removed Apollo's company page in March 2025; verify every address manually.
tools.status: changed: free tier reduced to 900 credits/year (75/month) in late-2026 captures

tools.name: Clay
tools.what: Go-to-market data enrichment and workflow orchestration platform.
tools.why: Built for commercial GTM sales teams with credit metering; Launch plan costs US$185/month on monthly billing or US$167/month billed annually (correcting T0-05's billing-basis error). Unnecessary at <=30 job-seeker sends/week.

tools.name: Hunter.io
tools.what: Work-email finder and verifier by company domain.
tools.why: Free tier provides 50 credits/month (Starter US$49/month monthly or US$34/month annual), covering roughly one-third of a 30-sends/week cadence (~130 new contacts/month); pair with manual pattern guessing and verification. Not in Pin's audit.

tools.name: Paid email finders (Wiza, ContactOut, Forager)
tools.what: Subscription tools that look up work emails for named individuals.
tools.why: Pin's 1.3M-lookup vendor audit found hit rates of 55.2% (Wiza), 48.2% (ContactOut) and 45.9% (Forager) versus 92-99% claimed, and hit rate is not deliverability. Free tiers plus pattern guessing suffice at <=30 sends/week.

tools.name: RocketReach
tools.what: Paid contact-lookup database.
tools.why: Lowest hit rate (29.8%) in Pin's 1.3M-lookup vendor audit against 92-99% vendor claims (hit rate is not deliverability), with annual-only paid plans at about US$396-399/year (up from US$329).

tools.name: LinkedIn connected apps
tools.what: Partner-verified tool activity displayed on LinkedIn profiles and surfaced in Hiring Assistant 2.
tools.why: Announced 2026-06-17 with no hiring-outcome evidence yet and new third-party data-sharing exposure; connect only relevant partners you trust.
tools.status: new: announced 2026-06-17; no outcome evidence

tools.name: LinkedIn Open to Work (recruiters-only and public frame)
tools.what: Profile status feeding Recruiter's Open to Work filter, plus India-only notice-period and salary fields.
tools.why: Recruiters-only puts you in the Recruiter filter (India added notice-period and expected-salary filters in October 2025), though LinkedIn cannot guarantee employer concealment. LinkedIn's 2x messages and +40% InMails claims date from 2020 with no method (C); stigma is unmeasured.

tools.name: LinkedIn Premium Career and Sales Navigator
tools.what: Paid LinkedIn tiers with InMail credits, applicant insights and advanced search filters.
tools.why: Premium Career is about US$29.99-39.99/month (5 InMails; US$39.99 cited by Texas AG); Sales Navigator Core is US$99.99-119.99 (50 InMails). LinkedIn's 3.9x hired claim on Top applicant jobs is uncontrolled (COI) with no independent evidence; trial one month at most and measure replies.
tools.status: under investigation: Texas AG CID issued 2026-07-14 over job listings and Premium marketing; no lawsuit found through 2026-09

tools.name: LinkedIn verification and colleague vouching
tools.what: Workplace email verification, optional government ID check and peer vouching (launched 2026-09-23).
tools.why: Low-cost signal surfaced in Hiring Assistant 2 candidate views (115M verified members and 700K+ companies reported 2026-09-23). LinkedIn's uplift claims (+60% views, +13% recruiter responses) give no method (C, likely selection); weigh personal-data exposure before ID checks.
tools.status: new: colleague vouching and admin removal of false employment claims launched 2026-09-23

tools.name: Third-party LinkedIn profile optimisers and AI rewriters
tools.what: Tools offering keyword scoring and AI-rewritten LinkedIn headlines or About sections.
tools.why: No outcome evidence; LinkedIn Recruiter AI-Assisted Search explicitly surfaces qualifications found and missed, so AI-padded profiles risk credibility failures during screening.

tools.name: ADPList
tools.what: Free-to-start mentorship marketplace (median completed session 30 minutes).
tools.why: Useful for free feedback, but counts conflict across its own pages (2026-11-12 stats page lists 39K+ mentors and 593K+ members vs undated About page 32K+ and 300K+) and its State of Mentorship reports topics rather than job outcomes.

tools.name: MentorCruise
tools.what: Paid 1:1 subscription mentorship (7-day free trial).
tools.why: Self-published page lists US$120-450/month plans, US$100-500/call and US$100-250/hour alongside conflicting mentor counts ('6k+' and '6,700+') and uncorroborated satisfaction claims. Pay only for structured learning, not job placement.

tools.name: LinkedIn engagement pod services and AI comment bots
tools.what: Coordinated reciprocal likes/comments and automated commenting tools.
tools.why: Against LinkedIn policy; LinkedIn added a 2025-08-20 Help rule limiting visibility of excessive or automated comments and confirmed it reduces reach for detected pods, with zero hiring evidence.

tools.name: Third-party LinkedIn automation (PhantomBuster and similar bots and scraping extensions)
tools.what: Tools that automate connection requests, messages or comments, or scrape profiles on LinkedIn.
tools.why: Hard disqualifier D2: prohibited by LinkedIn User Agreement section 8.2 with account restriction and comment visibility limits (2025-08-20). LinkedIn sued Proxycurl (resolved July 2025) and ProAPIs (October 2025), and CNIL fined Kaspr EUR 240,000 for scraping restricted LinkedIn contacts.

tools.name: Final Round AI (mock-interview mode)
tools.what: Paid and free-tier AI mock-interview practice mode sold alongside Final Round AI's live Interview Copilot.
tools.why: K21 contradicted T0-10: Trustpilot shows 2.8/5 on 280 reviews (2026-10-22; refund, billing, support and latency complaints), and the 2026-10-08 privacy policy permits audio, voice samples and screen captures to be used for AI training with human review and states no retention period. Mock-only efficacy unassessed.

tools.name: Google Interview Warmup
tools.what: Free browser-based behavioural and role Q&A practice tool launched by Google in 2022.

tools.name: Axial Search (US AI & ML salary reports)
tools.what: Published US posted-salary reports covering 43,480 AI-engineering and 13,776 ML-engineering postings (Jan–Oct 2026).
tools.why: Large US posted-range corpora (reporting top-of-band base ceilings, not midpoints). Recruiter COI, and its level-split equity mention shares are internally inconsistent, so rely on its salary ceilings only.

tools.name: Broad crowdsourced salary sites (Glassdoor, Payscale, Indeed, AmbitionBox)
tools.what: Employee-reported and posting-weighted salary averages for the wider market.
tools.why: A different population from Levels.fyi: India's broad market centres near ₹10–15L for AI engineers, against a Levels.fyi Bengaluru ML Engineer median of ₹44.5L. Use them as a population contrast, not for equity-bearing roles.

tools.name: Comprehensive.io
tools.what: Crawler of salary ranges posted on US tech career pages.
tools.why: Compensation database cited in Phase 0, but its live status was unverified in T0-44; the '14% of 43,480 US AI-engineering postings mention equity' figure belongs to Axial Search, not Comprehensive.io.
tools.status: unverified: live status not found in T0-44

tools.name: Levels.fyi salary database
tools.what: Crowdsourced total-compensation data by company, level, title and location, with structured exports.
tools.why: Anchor for big-tech and title total comp (Grade B); new-offer entries mix with realised stock. Prefer dated English Nov 2026 .md pages (which include n): Apr-Jul exports have unit/location bugs, non-English pages conflict on INR, tables mix average/median, small-n lab pages drift, and widgets are unfiltered.

tools.name: Pave (published reports)
tools.what: Employer-side compensation platform; candidates see only its published benchmarks.
tools.why: Employer-facing platform publishing Grade B/C compensation norms: May 2026 Merit Cycle puts non-promoted AI/ML raises at 4.4% vs 3.7% R&D and 3.4% overall (H1 2026 promotion rate 8.6%). T0-44 did not independently re-locate earlier 6.5% promoted-raise or +39% promotion-equity figures.

tools.name: Recruiter salary guides (Robert Half, Michael Page, Cooper Fitch, Hays)
tools.what: Placement-based or survey salary guides published by recruitment firms.
tools.why: Regional cross-checks only: Robert Half's Zurich page reports placement-based starting base excluding bonus, and Michael Page's UAE figures reached T0-02 only through relays. T0-02 advises against binding decisions on Gulf pay bands until primary data replace them.

tools.name: Third-party LCA browsers (Ellis, careery.pro, Visaverge, h1bdata.net, MyVisaJobs)
tools.what: Websites that process DOL H-1B filings into employer and title pages.
tools.why: Cross-check only: methods differ, and one aggregator's two OpenAI pages gave San Francisco medians of $180K and $310K. Treat their output as indicative until the raw DOL file is reproduced.

tools.name: US DOL OFLC LCA disclosure files
tools.what: Official quarterly H-1B wage filings by employer, job title and offered wage range.
tools.why: A base-wage floor and a within-employer title comparison, not pay: base only, visa-sponsored roles only, titles such as 'Member of Technical Staff' hide seniority, and some filers set range floors at the legal minimum. Process the raw files yourself.

tools.name: AI Incident Database and OECD AI incidents monitor
tools.what: Searchable repositories of reported AI incidents.
tools.why: AIID holds 1,460 human-mediated incidents; OECD AIM is labelled Beta with AI-generated summaries/classifications from news clusters (9,218 incidents + 5,312 hazards in arXiv snapshot; ~17,104 on AIM page). Verify AIM entries against primary sources.

tools.name: danluu/post-mortems
tools.what: GitHub collection of public postmortems.
tools.why: Categorised public postmortem archive (config, hardware, conflicts, time, database) with entries into 2026; infrastructure-heavy with few AI-product cases, so pair with AIID and employer history.

tools.name: Evidently AI ML and LLM system design database
tools.what: Searchable collection of company case studies on ML and LLM systems.
tools.why: 800+ production ML/LLM use cases from 185 companies (2025-12-22 blog; cached database header lags at 650 / 2025-08-14). Vendor-maintained self-reports with no independent outcome verification; useful for prior art, not as proof of ROI.

tools.name: Bonterms Professional Services Agreement
tools.what: Open standard professional services contract cover page and terms.
tools.why: v1.2 cover page offers licensed or assigned deliverables and is listed as CC0-1.0 on OpenAgreements, while other Bonterms standards use CC BY-ND; full PSA standard terms were not retrieved. Verify licence and terms with counsel.

tools.name: Common Paper standard agreements
tools.what: Free CC BY 4.0 contract standards: a Professional Services Agreement (v1.1), NDAs and an AI Addendum (v1.0).
tools.why: T0-18's base template; its services agreement sets general and increased liability caps on the cover page. The AI Addendum covers data usage, training rights, IP and liability, but its clause text was not retrieved. Have AI, IP and liability terms reviewed by a lawyer.

tools.name: Freelancers Union Contract Creator
tools.what: Free beta generator for contracts covering scope, payment terms and deadlines.
tools.why: No IP clause is mentioned, so it is too thin for AI work: in India a contractor is the first owner of the code, and an assignment silent on duration and territory defaults to five years and India only.

tools.name: OpenAgreements
tools.what: Free library of 125 contract templates, including Common Paper's.
tools.why: Good for browsing and comparing templates; each template keeps its source licence, and the site calls itself legal research, not legal advice.

tools.name: Deel (employer of record and contractor payments)
tools.what: Employer-of-record, contractor-management and contractor-of-record services.
tools.why: Pricing page (read in T0-43) lists EOR from $599/employee-mo, contractors $49 and CoR from $325; third-party tables report a 1-month deposit and 0.6–2% FX margin (C). EOR removes direct misclassification risk, not dependent-agent PE risk (Deel guidance, C). Rippling v. Deel litigation is proceeding (Feb & Sep 2026 rulings, B).
tools.status: changed: Rippling v. Deel litigation proceeding (Feb & Sep 2026 rulings)

tools.name: India-specialist EORs (Wisemonk, Remunance, Gloroots)
tools.what: India-focused employer-of-record providers offering local statutory payroll wrappers.
tools.why: Vendor sites quote $99–$399 per employee a month — well below global EOR fees — when hiring exclusively in India, but all evidence comes from vendor marketing (COI) with no independent audit of escrow, compliance or financial stability.

tools.name: Multiplier
tools.what: APAC-strong employer-of-record and contractor-management platform.
tools.why: Third-party comparison tables and vendor guides quote standalone EOR around $400–$500 per employee a month without a mandatory HRIS base fee, but official pricing was not opened directly; verify India statutory pass-throughs and deposits directly.

tools.name: Oyster (employer of record)
tools.what: Global employer-of-record and contractor-management platform.
tools.why: Published EOR pricing at $699 per employee a month ($599 appears only in older third-party tables) and contractors at $29 a month (T0-43 Extract, B/C). Indian statutory pass-throughs (EPF, professional tax, gratuity) bill on top of the subscription.

tools.name: Papaya Global
tools.what: Fintech-oriented global payroll, EOR and Contractor of Record platform with owned payment rails.
tools.why: Third-party tables report EOR from ~$499 per employee a month, Contractor of Record from ~$199 and global payroll from ~$29 (C); direct vendor quote needed for India statutory pass-throughs and FX margins.

tools.name: Pebl (formerly Velocity Global)
tools.what: Enterprise-focused global employer-of-record platform (rebranded from Velocity Global).
tools.why: Third-party and vendor guides report standalone EOR starting from $399 per employee a month after Velocity Global's rebrand to Pebl; exact India pass-throughs, FX spreads and deposit terms require a direct quote.
tools.status: renamed: Velocity Global rebranded to Pebl

tools.name: Remote (employer of record)
tools.what: Employer-of-record, contractor-management and contractor-of-record service operating owned local entities.
tools.why: $599 per employee a month on annual billing or $699 month-to-month; contractor management $29, Plus $99 ($100k indemnity), CoR from $325 (B). Owned-entity structure appeals to IP-sensitive employers. Against India presumptive taxation (s.58(2)), an EOR cuts take-home by 22–24% up to ₹75L and reaches near parity near ₹1.2Cr; value lies in statutory benefits and lower misclassification risk, not tax or PE elimination.

tools.name: Rippling EOR
tools.what: Employer-of-record module layered on Rippling's unified HR, payroll and IT platform.
tools.why: Quote-based EOR reported from $499+ per employee a month on top of Rippling's core platform base fee ($8+/user/month, third-party tables, C); practical mainly when the employer already runs Rippling HR/IT. Active Rippling v. Deel litigation is proceeding (B).
tools.status: changed: Rippling v. Deel litigation proceeding (Feb & Sep 2026 rulings)

tools.name: AI-training and expert-data platforms (Mercor, Scale AI / Outlier, Surge)
tools.what: Contract marketplaces paying engineers and domain experts to author prompts, evaluations and RLHF/post-training data.
tools.why: Fast remote onboarding for supplemental income, but weak worker protections and active misclassification litigation (including a Mercor class action covering ~30,000 workers alongside April 2026 breach reports; Handshake AI roles are US-only; B/C). Treat as short-term cashflow filler only, never primary career employment.
tools.status: changed: misclassification lawsuits reported against Mercor, Scale and Surge

tools.name: Alignerr (Labelbox)
tools.what: Labelbox's freelance 1099 AI-training network for verified PhD and domain experts.
tools.why: 1099 hourly contracts with verified-education screening and no visa sponsorship; explicitly notes rates may vary outside the US (older copy $15-$150/hr).

tools.name: Handshake AI
tools.what: Part-time domain-expert and red-teaming AI training contracts.
tools.why: Red-teaming domain expert listed at $40-$60/hr for 10-20 hours/week (older occupation-titled listings $75-$125/hr); 15-30 min AI/recruiter screen; STEM OPT not supported.

tools.name: Mercor
tools.what: Standing expert-talent pools contracting domain specialists and engineers for AI lab evaluation and training.
tools.why: Standing pools (3/3 read listings), not vacancies; ~20-min AI interview, $35-$200/hr listed bands, weekly independent-contractor pay, projects can end early, no H-1B/STEM OPT. Headline averages unstable ($80-$141). March 2026 LiteLLM supply-chain breach exposed ~4 TB of contractor IDs/W-9s/video interviews (live-verified 2026-11-19).
tools.status: under investigation: March 2026 LiteLLM supply-chain data breach and federal class actions (live-verified 2026-11-19)

tools.name: micro1
tools.what: AI-recruiter vetted contractor platform for AI evaluation specialists and domain experts.
tools.why: Global-remote AI Evaluation Specialist listed at $20-$35/hr; US education/tutoring $50-$100/hr; screens via AI video recruiter; referral aggregator reports median 51 days to hire and 2% placement (24/1,091, D).

tools.name: Outlier (Scale AI)

tools.name: Scale AI Human Frontier Collective
tools.what: Selective US-only part-time research-advisor programme for credentialled medical, legal and finance experts.
tools.why: Posted $300/hr for 5-20 hours/week requiring 5+ years and MD/DO, JD/bar or finance depth; rolling application plus research-team interview with 90-day re-apply wait; US-only.

tools.name: Turing (Domain Expert Reviewer / AI Training)

tools.name: Braintrust
tools.what: Enterprise talent network for freelance engagements.
tools.why: 0% talent fee and 100% on clients you bring; competitor/directory sources report a 10-15% client fee and a 15% full-time conversion fee within six months (vendor fee page not opened).

tools.what: Expert marketplace for enterprise consulting projects.
